name: The five deadly acts (ānantarya)

names.name: wuni 五逆 — excluded in the 18th vow yet admitted in the lowest grade

description: Killing mother, father or an arhat, dividing the Saṅgha, wounding a Buddha with evil intent; they ripen in hell in the next life; the schism-lie is the gravest.

name: Rejecting the true dharma (saddharmapratikṣepa)

names.name: bangfa 謗法: graver than the five offences because it rejects the very Dharma (Tanluan)

description: Denying that the Mahāyāna sūtras are the Buddha's word; a karma worse than the five deadly acts, excluded from the eighteenth vow, and the mark of the icchantika.

name: The five turbidities (pañcakaṣāya)

names.name: wuzhuo e'shi 五濁惡世 — the age in which only the Pure Land gate is passable

description: Degeneracy of the aeon, beings, defilements, views and lifespan, in which the Buddha teaches by skillful means.

name: Doubting the Buddha's wisdom

names.name: giwaku; doubt keeps us in birth-and-death (Shōshinge on Hōnen)

description: Cultivating merit and aspiring to birth while doubting the Buddha's inconceivable wisdom: such beings are born in the womb-palace or borderland, not seeing the Buddha for five hundred years; if one plants good roots but doubts, the lotus does not open.
antidotes: clear faith in the Buddha's wisdom (Larger Sūtra)

equivalents.note: doubt as a hindrance vs doubt of the Buddha's vow specifically

name: Arrogance, corruption and laziness (that hinder faith)
description: The arrogant, corrupt and lazy find it hard to believe this teaching; evil beings of wrong views and arrogance find joyful trust the hardest of difficulties.

name: The five evils, five pains and five burnings
description: The Larger Sūtra's account of the evils of this world and their painful and burning retributions, among which the Buddha teaches: (1) the strong oppress the weak, killing and devouring one another; (2) family members and officials without righteousness deceive, cheat and covet; (3) lust and illicit desire; (4) double tongue, harsh words, lies, frivolous talk, slander of the good, unfilial conduct; (5) idleness, neglect of family and parents, and indulgence in drink and food.
notes: Openings of the five sections read locally in T360; content summarised from their opening lines.

name: Mixed (miscellaneous) practice
description: Abandoning exclusive practice for mixed practices: mind disturbed by conditions, not in accord with the vow, recollection not continuous, dedication not earnest, passions intervening, no shame or repentance, no gratitude, pride and pursuit of fame, no good companions — hardly one or two in a hundred are born; the mixed stop in the land of sloth.

name: The three kinds of non-faith (Tanluan)
description: Faith that is not genuine, not single and not continuous — why calling the name may not break ignorance; they entail one another.
antidotes: the three faiths: genuine, single, continuous

name: The rivers of water and fire (greed and anger)
description: In Shandao's parable the river of water is beings' greed and the river of fire their anger, lapping the narrow white path of aspiration.

name: Confusion and loss of right mindfulness at death
description: The pains of death ('the wind-knife') scatter the unpractised mind; the presence of those who have taken wine or meat brings loss of right mindfulness and deranged death.

name: Licensed evil (zōaku muge)
description: The view that since the vow saves the evil one may freely do evil; rejected by Hōnen's pledge and Shinran's letters ('do not take poison because there is an antidote').

name: Self-power calculation (hakarai)
description: Relying on one's own judgement and good to secure birth — the mind of self-power which obstructs entrusting; 'no working is true working'.

name: The heresy of 'settled ten kalpas ago' (jikkō anjin)
description: The view that birth was already settled when Amida attained buddhahood ten kalpas ago, so that no entrusting is now needed; rejected by Rennyo.

name: Secret teachings (hiji bōmon)
description: Teachings transmitted in secret at night outside the public teaching (as Zenran claimed); rejected by Shinran and Rennyo.
